newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV DIPS TO 1,496-1,500 PER DLR AT CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV DIPS TO 1,496-1,500 PER DLR AT CLOSE.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,496-1,500 per dollar on Monday, a touch softer from the opening's 1,493-1,497 due to a rise in dollar demand on the interbank market, dealers said.
"Final clients started bidding for dollars and the lev eased by around three (levs against the dollar) from the opening. Trade was calm," a commercial bank dealer said.

The central bank was also seen bidding for dollars, containing a lev rise amid increased foreign currency supply from local and foreign investors eyeing high-yield lev-denominated government securities, traders said.
The Finance ministry offered four floating interest T-bill issues with maturities of three, six, nine and 12 months and no par value or minimum acceptable price set in advance at auctions today.
Settlement for the auctions falls on Wednesday, the value date of today's spot-deals, dealers said.

Interest on the paper is linked to the central bank main interest rate and is adjusted every time the rate changes. The main rate is now set at 6.20 percent monthly. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
